sources.description: The Voodoo Lab Giggity goes beyond overdrive. It's an analog preamp that transforms any rig and gives you tones you can't get anywhere else.
sources.snippet: Voodoo Lab Giggity Review: Beyond Overdrive
sources.bodyExcerpt: Voodoo Lab Giggity Review: Beyond Overdrive Home - Voodoo Lab HOME PRODUCTS POWER Pedal Power ® 2 PLUS Pedal Power ® 3 Pedal Power ® 3 PLUS Pedal Power ® 4×4 Pedal Power ® ISO-5 Pedal Power ® MONDO Pedal Power ® X4 Expander Kit Pedal Power ® X8 Pedal Power ® X4 Pedal Power ® X4-18V Expander Kit Pedal Power ® X4-18V PEDALBOARDS Dingbat ® PX Pedalboard with PX-8 PLUS Pedal Switcher Dingbat ® Large Dingbat ® Medium Dingbat ® Small-EX Dingbat ® Small Dingbat ® TINY SWITCHING Amp Selector ABY Isolated Output Switch/Blend Amp Selector PRO Isolated Output Switch/Blend Control Switcher MIDI Amp Commander GCX True Bypass 8-Loop Rackmount Audio Switcher Ground Control Pro MIDI Foot Controller HEX True Bypass 6-Loop Audio Switcher PX-8 PLUS True Bypass Programmable Pedal Switcher EFFECTS GIGGITY ® Analog Overdrive + Preamp Sparkle Drive ® MOD Superfuzz ® ACCESSORIES Cables Mounting Brackets Power Switcher Accessories Pedalboard Accessories Merch Apparel PURCHASE UNITED STATES CANADA INTERNATIONAL ONLINE QUICK ORDER ARTISTS BLOG SUPPORT REGISTER YOUR PRODUCT USER GROUP MANUALS CONTACT US ABOUT Quick Order Manuals Contact Account Privacy Policy Return Policy Terms & Conditions ✕ Add a Second Channel to your Amp June 24, 2026 The Ultimate Guide to Guitar Effects Switching Systems MIDI Control June 24, 2026 Add a Second Channel to your Amp June 24, 2026 The Ultimate Guide to Guitar Effects Switching Systems MIDI Control June 24, 2026 Published by Darrin Fox at June 24, 2026 Categories Product Demos Tags preamp Giggity SIgnal Chain Tone Tips overdrive The Secret Weapon Your Signal Chain Is Missing Learn how the Voodoo Lab Giggity delivers the tone you’ve been chasing. In a sea of copycat overdrive pedals, the Voodoo Lab Giggity ® Analog Overdrive + Preamp stands alone. In this video, James Santiago shows you how Giggity goes beyond your average dirt pedal, delivering “analog mastering” detail and vibe to any rig. No matter your guitar, amp, or effects, Giggity gives you tones unobtainable with any other pedal. Breaking Down the Controls 1. Loudness for Preamp Voicing This is the input gain for Giggity’s preamp section. You can use a low setting for cleaner tones or turn it all the way up for some grit and compression making a stiff amp come alive under your fingers. 2. Surgical Tone Shaping with Body Air Beyond traditional bass and treble controls, use Giggity’s Body and Air to fine tune your tones. Body: From taming an “ice-pick” bridge pickup to clearing up a muddy humbucker or adding weight to a Strat’s rear pickup, Body boosts or cuts lower midrange/upper bass frequencies. Air: Add shimmer and clarity that’s impossible to get with a standard presence or treble control without introducing harshness. 3. Add Final Touch with Sun/Moon Switch Giving you magic in four positions, Sun/Moon changes the entire gain structure of the preamp. Sun: Bright and alive — open the curtain, move towards the sun. Moon: Cooler and thick— add weight and depth, lean to the dark. 4. Master for Output Volume Adjusts Giggity’s overall level to your amp. Crank to push your amp into rough n’ ready overdrive or back down to unity gain for more transparency. Giggity ® Analog Overdrive + Preamp FAQ Where should I put the Giggity in my signal chain? You can use Giggity two ways: Up Front: Place it first to “pre-master” your guitar’s pickups, shaping how your overdrives and everything downstream react to your playing. At the End: Place it last to shape your overall tone before hitting your amp. This is also the best way to dial in an unfamiliar backline amp. Does Giggity replace my Overdrive? Not necessarily. While the Loudness knob will add some grit, Giggity is designed to make your existing overdrives — and everything else — sound better . Is Giggity true bypass? Yes. Like all Voodoo Lab pedals, Giggity features true-bypass switching via high-reliability gold-contact relays. —Darrin Fox Share Darrin Fox Related posts June 24, 20

The Voodoo Lab Superfuzz is based on the ultra-rare, 1968 Jordan Electronics Bosstone. Superfuzz takes this classic fuzz design and adds tone and resonance circuits so you can dial up an amazing array of new tones. What does the Tone control do? The Tone control delivers a wide spectrum of midrange and bass timbres. You can dial in everything from an extremely scooped to raucous, bluesy midrange voicings. What does the Resonance control do? The Resonance control is a unique sub-harmonic booster that lets you add an aggressive bottom end not typically found on fuzz pedals. What does the Attack control do? The Attack knob varies the gain from rich and creamy to outrageous. Does the Superfuzz have True Bypass switching? Yes. In fact, all Voodoo Lab pedals have True Bypass switching giving you absolutely no loss of tone when the pedal is bypassed. What kind of external power jack does it have? Current Superfuzz pedals with the LED have a 5.5 x 2.1mm barrel connector. However, older Voodoo Lab pedals without the LED have a 3.5mm mini-plug jack. How much current do Voodoo Lab pedals draw? sources.bodyExcerpt: Proctavia FAQ - Voodoo Lab Home - Voodoo Lab HOME PRODUCTS POWER Pedal Power ® 2 PLUS Pedal Power ® 3 Pedal Power ® 3 PLUS Pedal Power ® 4×4 Pedal Power ® ISO-5 Pedal Power ® MONDO Pedal Power ® X4 Expander Kit Pedal Power ® X8 Pedal Power ® X4 Pedal Power ® X4-18V Expander Kit Pedal Power ® X4-18V PEDALBOARDS Dingbat ® PX Pedalboard with PX-8 PLUS Pedal Switcher Dingbat ® Large Dingbat ® Medium Dingbat ® Small-EX Dingbat ® Small Dingbat ® TINY SWITCHING Amp Selector ABY Isolated Output Switch/Blend Amp Selector PRO Isolated Output Switch/Blend Control Switcher MIDI Amp Commander GCX True Bypass 8-Loop Rackmount Audio Switcher Ground Control Pro MIDI Foot Controller HEX True Bypass 6-Loop Audio Switcher PX-8 PLUS True Bypass Programmable Pedal Switcher EFFECTS GIGGITY ® Analog Overdrive + Preamp Sparkle Drive ® MOD Superfuzz ® ACCESSORIES Cables Mounting Brackets Power Switcher Accessories Pedalboard Accessories Merch Apparel PURCHASE UNITED STATES CANADA INTERNATIONAL ONLINE QUICK ORDER ARTISTS BLOG SUPPORT REGISTER YOUR PRODUCT USER GROUP MANUALS CONTACT US ABOUT Quick Order Manuals Contact Account Privacy Policy Return Policy Terms & Conditions ✕ What is the Proctavia? The Voodoo Lab Proctavia is an exact replica of Tycobrahe Sound Company’s Octavia which is a fuzz/octave pedal that creates a note an octave higher than the original. Considered to be one of the most desired pedals by vintage collectors, the sound of the Octavia is what gave the solo in ”Purple Haze” its unique, stringy sting. How close is the Proctavia to an old Octavia? The Proctavia is an exact replica that includes the same transistors, germanium diodes and transformer coupled output stage as the original circuit. Why does mine sound broken? When you first try the Proctavia, if you merely plug it in and strum a chord, you will hear a dissonant distortion that sounds like it’s broken. You need to learn to play the Proctavia like a new instrument. As a general rule, single note solos lines are fine. Chords, unless they are of the harmonically simple power chord-type, can be a little more difficult to navigate. Chords through the Proctavia can be the coolest and worst sounds you’ll ever hear. Use this power with caution grasshopper. Can I use it with a power supply like the DC Brick? No. Like other Octavia pedals that are around, the Proctavia pedal is a positive ground. It can run on a battery, on its own power supply (like the Boss PSA-120), or with the Pedal Power units (because the outputs are isolated). However, it will shut down the whole power supply if it is fed into an output that is not isolated. Most other multi-output power supplies (Dunlop DC Brick, Godlyke, daisy chained Boss) have a common ground which means that the outputs aren’t individually regulated. If you have other negative ground pedals being powered with one of these multi-output power supplies, the Proctavia pedal will not work. What kind of external power jack does it have? Current Proctavia pedals with the LED have a 5.5×2.1mm barrel connector. However, older Voodoo Lab pedals without the LED have a 3.5mm mini-plug jack. How much current do Voodoo Lab pedals draw? None of our pedals draw more than 50mA. What are the dimensions of Voodoo Lab pedals? The dimensions of the pedals are: L 4 3/4″ x W 3 3/4″ x H 2″ Where is the serial number on Voodoo Lab pedals? Shipping Info Refund and Returns Policy Scrapbook of Memories Current Feature Feature Archive News of the Day Hours and Contact Shop New Instruments Used Instruments Books Accessories Pickups and Electronics Gift Cards Shipping Info Services Rentals Events Friends Of Old Time Jam Tune List Event Archives Lessons Links 0 items $0.00 Menu Cart Home / Miscellaneous - Used / Voodoo Labs Proctavia Voodoo Labs Proctavia $ 135.00 Voodoo Labs Proctavia quantity Add to cart SKU: CON-ISI12204 Category: Miscellaneous - Used Tag: Voodoo Labs Description Reviews (0) Description The Octavia is a fuzz which creates the octave doubling effect (one octave higher) made famous by Jimi Hendrix and Jeff Beck. The Voodoo Lab Proctavia is an exact replica of Tycobrahe Sound Company’s Octavia, the model used by Stevie Ray Vaughan and considered the most desirable by vintage collectors. The Proctavia includes the same transistors, germanium diodes and transformer coupled output stage as the original circuit to produce the outrageous distortion and high octave sound heard on classic recordings like “Are You Experienced” and “Wired.” “Voodoo Lab’s Proctavia: it’ll put a spell on you.” “Once the Proctavia is plugged in, it doesn’t take long to realise that you’re dealing with a quality pedal that oozes versatility from its two controls.” – WHAT GUITAR Magazine, U.K. CLASSIC SETTINGS Basic Octavia – Set the Boost all the way down and the Volume at about 1/2. Use the bridge pickup on your guitar. Back down your guitar volume a little. Play single notes at least halfway up the neck. You will get best results with new strings. Also, try hitting strings with the edge of your pick to emphasize harmonics. Super-long Sustain – Turn your guitar volume and the Boost all the way up. Set the Volume to the desired level. Play single notes for solos. This pedal is in very good condition. Power supply not included. Made in USA True bypass switch Volume and Boost knobs Reviews There are no reviews yet. Its overdrive circuit provides the same tone as a vintage ‘808. Then the clean control blends back in a boosted direct signal. This restores the attack and feel which is lost in a highly compressed overdrive circuit. The Sparkle Drive utilizes the same concept as layering two amps, one clean and the other saturated. Of course with the clean control turned down, you get a classic overdrive tone. All the way up, it provides a super transparent, 100% clean boost. And just like every Voodoo Lab pedal effect, the Sparkle Drive features true bypass switching, a heavy-duty metal switch and on/off status LED. It’s hand built from the finest components available and is backed by a 5-year warranty. $ 129.99 FIND A DEALER Your browser does not support the audio element. (386g) Power Requirements 9V DC, 20mA Power Input Type 5.5mm x 2.1mm barrel connector, center negative polarity Product ID VD Warranty 5-year limited warranty in North America. It has no effect on the “clean” signal. Use low settings to warm up and compress your tone. Turn it up for additional sustain and saturation. TONE – Turn it up for a brighter sound, down for darker. It is for the overdrive only and has no effect on the “clean” signal. CLEAN – Blends the boosted clean signal with the overdrive. All the way down is overdrive only. All the way up is clean only. In between is a blend of both clean and overdrive. VOLUME – Sets the output level. sources.bodyExcerpt: Bulldog Distortion by VOX | RockBoard | PedalPedia Skip to main content LOG IN EXPLORE VOX Bulldog Distortion LOG IN TO SUGGEST IMPROVEMENTS DISTORTION Description The effect pedals in the COOLTRON series are clearly pedal mines of a special kind. After all, they contain a genuine 12AU7 preamp tube, which stands for bite, warmth and tons of fat, but is still not a battery guzzler. A power supply unit is an optional extra in the truest sense of the word: nice, but not indispensable. Two channels - each with its own GAIN and level control - with a wonderfully growly tube sound. The name says it all: with the VOX Bulldog Distortion, you'll scorch the hair of even the fans in the back row. “Gain 1” covers the ‘vintage’ distortion range, while “Gain 2”, in keeping with the spirit of the times, is more aggressive and has slightly emphasized mids. Both modes can be roared from “subtle” to “completely sick”. And if you want it to thump with a high level of exaggeration, simply turn the BASS control up further. With less drive, on the other hand, it provides an additional boost of warmth. With the VOICE control of “Gain 2”, you can then add those sandpaper applications to the sound where the wallpaper comes off the walls even three blocks away. Finally, the TREBLE control is used to round off or pimp up the irresistible sound. The Bulldog pedal is equipped with a true bypass circuit. As is well known, tubes require a voltage that a battery-powered effect pedal has not yet been able to handle. Countless inventors have already attempted to address a tube using the less-is-more method. However, this only works to a limited extent, because a tube does not like to play under a tariff and is then stingy with the sound. Their power consumption is far higher than what a battery can withstand for more than a few minutes. And your audience isn't paying for your battery changing skills on stage! For this reason alone, the COOLTRONs are really cool. The COOLTRON circuit is based on two unconventional signal paths: a “servo circuit” that creates the right atmosphere between the plate and the grid in the tube, thus ensuring stable conditions in which the tube can flourish without restriction; and a patented power supply that feeds the tube's heating elements with economical low voltage. As the tube runs on a low flame, so to speak, the anode current is far below the control value. This in turn means that the cathode no longer needs as much heat to supply a sufficient amount of current. This is why the 4 AA batteries in the COOLTRON pedals have a sensational service life of 18 hours! local Find online Documents SPECS Specs PHOTOS Photos Product Description Valvenergy – Copperhead Drive Iconic amp sounds for your pedalboard. The Copperhead Drive valve distortion pedal offers the powerful crunch of British full stack amps in a compact pedal format, powered by Nutube for warm and responsive amp-like tones. Inspired by thick and punchy British amp tones, the Copperhead Drive goes beyond the amp-in-a-box category to offer a truly flexible valve distortion pedal. The all-analog signal path and Nutube allow for genuine overdrive and distortion tones with the feel of a real tube amp, while internally boosted voltage gives greater headroom and dynamics. Plus, the OLED display shows an oscilloscope while the pedal is active or bypassed, allowing you to understand exactly how your signal is affected. Three output modes allow you to use this as a standard pedal, a line-level preamp, and a direct amp-sim using the built-in analog cabinet simulator. Use STANDARD mode with your normal guitar rig to totally transform your amp, or use PREAMP or CAB-SIM mode while recording directly into your audio interface. In each mode, the all-analog design and active EQ allow you to perfectly dial in the sound you need in any situation. The Cutting Edge valve distortion pedal offers aggressive saturated and precise modern metal tones in a compact pedal format, powered by Nutube for warm and responsive amp-like tones. Inspired by the meticulous and tight tones heard on modern metal records, the Cutting Edge goes beyond the amp-in-a-box category to offer a truly flexible valve distortion pedal. The all-analog signal path and Nutube allow for genuine overdrive and distortion tones with the feel of a real tube amp, while internally boosted voltage gives greater headroom and dynamics. Three output modes allow you to use this as a standard pedal, a line-level preamp, and a direct amp-sim using the built-in analog cabinet simulator. Use STANDARD mode with your normal guitar rig to totally transform your amp, or use PREAMP or CAB-SIM mode while recording directly into your audio interface. In each mode, the all-analog design and active EQ allow you to perfectly dial in the sound you need in any situation. The Channel Link feature allows you to chain two or more Valvenergy pedals together, through the Link jack of each pedal. Using a with a standard 1/8 stereo cable will link 2 pedals, and using a stereo 1/8 splitter will link 3 or 4 pedals. This allows you to turn one pedal on while bypassing the others, as if you were switching between channels of a guitar amp. These pedals are equipped with a high-contrast OLED display showing an oscilloscope, a visual indication of how the waveform is affected by the knob settings. This display allows shows which mode you are currently using. Overdrive with Distinct Tube-like Response and Rich Harmonics, Featuring Organic Distortion FUEL INJECTOR offers a distinctive overdrive with clean characteristics, rich harmonics, and a natural sense of compression and bite. Developed by amp manufacturer VOX, this overdrive pedal stands out for its amp-like distortion, in contrast to typical pedal distortions. Unlike effects that color the tone like preamp-style pedals, FUEL INJECTOR preserves its natural characteristics while distorting through Nutube, providing a tone that sounds as if your connected amp is pushed into even more distortion. Compared to many drive pedals, including TS-style ones, it features overwhelming harmonic components and a pronounced compression characteristic reminiscent of a tube amp. The harmonic richness created by distorting Nutube in multiple stages, along with the bias variations unique to tubes, produces a resonant tone, capturing the essence of an amp-like sound. This characteristic allows for a pleasant drive sound when utilizing this pedal with a clean amp setting. FUEL INJECTOR adds a “resilience” to the sound, lifting up gracefully even during bends, ensuring that the player’s expression is conveyed seamlessly. Whether driving a clean amp with this pedal or using it as a booster for a slightly crunchy amp, it will undoubtedly prove powerful and effective. read more Controls DRIVE: Adjusts the amount of distortion. TONE: Adjusts the high-frequency content. LEVEL: Controls the output volume. Switch: Allows you to choose between two modes. NATURAL: The fundamental mode. FAT: Delivers a thicker tone, ideal when combined with single-coil pickups. Maximizing the characteristics of Nutube, a pedal series that brings out the unique features of combined equipment. The Valvenergy series has been well received as a pedal series that delivers the response of a tube amp, and now four new models are added to the lineup. sources.title: Vox VE-FI Valvenergy Fuel Injector Overdrive Effects Pedal | Firehouse Guitars
sources.description: FUEL INJECTOR offers a distinctive overdrive with clean characteristics, rich harmonics, and a natural sense of compression and bite. Developed by amp manufacturer VOX, this overdrive pedal stands out for its amp-like distortion, in contrast to typical pedal distortions. Unlike effects that color the tone like preamp-style pedals, FUEL INJECTOR preserves its natural characteristics while distorting through Nutube, providing a tone that sounds as if your connected amp is pushed into even more distortion. Compared to many drive pedals, including TS-style ones, it features overwhelming harmonic components and a pronounced compression characteristic reminiscent of a tube amp. The harmonic richness created by distorting Nutube in multiple stages, along with the bias variations unique to tubes, produces a resonant tone, capturing the essence of an amp-like sound. This characteristic allows for a pleasant drive sound when utilizing this pedal with a clean amp setting. FUEL INJECTOR adds a “resilience” to the sound, lifting up gracefully even during bends, ensuring that the player’s expression is conveyed seamlessly. Whether driving a clean amp with this pedal or using it as a booster for a slightly crunchy amp, it will undoubtedly prove powerful and effective.

sources.bodyExcerpt: Vox Ice 9 Overdrive Pedal Review: Honest Tone, Build Use Analysis | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Vox Ice 9 Overdrive Pedal Review: Honest Tone, Build Use Analysis By zoe-langford June 15, 2026 Vox Amplification Ice 9 Overdrive Pedal Review The Vox Ice 9 overdrive pedal delivers a refined, amp-like saturation with transparent gain staging and strong midrange articulation—making it a compelling option for players seeking dynamic, touch-sensitive overdrive without aggressive clipping or high-end fizz. It excels in clean-boost and light-to-moderate breakup applications, especially with vintage-style amps (like VOX AC30s or Fender Twins), but falls short as a high-gain lead driver or low-noise platform for complex pedalboards. This Vox Ice 9 overdrive pedal review evaluates its tonal authenticity, construction integrity, and practical utility across studio, rehearsal, and live contexts—not as a ‘magic box,’ but as a purpose-built tool with defined strengths and limitations. About Vox Amplification Ice 9 Overdrive Pedal Review Vox Amplification—a British brand with deep roots in guitar history since the 1950s—reintroduced the Ice 9 in 2019 as part of its modern boutique line, developed in collaboration with UK-based circuit designer Pete Cornish. Unlike Vox’s earlier overdrives (e.g., the 2000s Valvetronix series), the Ice 9 uses discrete JFET transistors instead of op-amps or digital modeling, aiming for analog warmth and dynamic response reminiscent of late-’60s germanium boosters and early ’70s silicon overdrives. Its name references both the Kurt Vonnegut novel (implying structural rigidity and cascading effect) and Vox’s own legacy “Ice” preamp topology used in select AC-series amplifiers. The pedal targets players who prioritize feel and harmonic complexity over saturated distortion—and who value Vox’s signature mid-forward voicing without the compression typical of many mid-priced overdrives. First Impressions Unboxing reveals a compact, brushed-aluminum enclosure measuring 118 × 73 × 50 mm—slightly larger than a standard Boss unit but smaller than most full-size boutique pedals. The chassis feels dense and rigid, with no panel flex or seam gaps. The matte black finish resists fingerprints, and the recessed LED indicator (blue when active) avoids stage glare. Controls are arranged left-to-right: Level , Drive , Tone , and Blend . All knobs use conductive plastic with tactile detents—firm but smooth, with clear 12 o’clock center markings. Input/output jacks are top-mounted, angled for cable management, and soldered directly to the PCB (not chassis-mounted). No battery compartment is included; it requires a regulated 9V DC supply (center-negative, 100 mA minimum)—a deliberate choice to ensure consistent headroom and noise rejection. Detailed Specifications The Ice 9’s spec sheet reflects intentional design tradeoffs. It is not a feature-rich multi-mode device, but a focused analog circuit optimized for transparency and responsiveness: Power Requirement: 9V DC, center-negative, ≥100 mA (no battery option) Current Draw: 32 mA (measured at 9V) Input Impedance: 1 MΩ (standard passive guitar input) Output Impedance: 500 Ω (low-Z, compatible with buffered and true-bypass loops) Circuit Type: Discrete Class-A JFET front-end (2SK372/2SJ103 complementary pair), followed by dual-stage clipping and passive tone network Bypass: True bypass (mechanical relay switch, audible click) Clipping Diodes: Dual asymmetrical silicon diodes (1N4148) + soft-clipping JFET stage Gain Range: Approx. −2 dB to +18 dB (clean boost to medium overdrive) Frequency Response: 20 Hz – 18 kHz (−3 dB points, measured into 10 kΩ load) Crucially, the Ice 9 does not include internal dip switches, expression inputs, preset memory, or MIDI—consistent with its philosophy of ‘one circuit, one voice.’ Sound Quality and Performance Tonal character is where the Ice 9 distinguishes itself. sources.description: A detailed, measurement-backed review of the Vox ICE 9 Overdrive pedal — evaluating its transparent gain staging, dual-mode architecture, JFET-based preamp topology, and real-world performance with Fender Stratocasters, Gibson Les Pauls, and Marshall, Fender, and Vox amplifiers.

sources.bodyExcerpt: Vox Amplification ICE 9 Overdrive Pedal Review: Precision Clarity and Dynamic Headroom in a Compact Stompbox | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Vox Amplification ICE 9 Overdrive Pedal Review: Precision Clarity and Dynamic Headroom in a Compact Stompbox By Nina Harper July 16, 2026 The Vox ICE 9 Overdrive is not another generic mid-gain booster — it’s a meticulously engineered, dual-path overdrive pedal designed for players who demand tonal fidelity, dynamic responsiveness, and studio-grade headroom. Built around discrete JFET circuitry (specifically Toshiba 2SK370 and 2SJ109 matched pairs), it delivers up to 25 dB of clean boost and 28 dB of musical overdrive with less than 0.08% THD at unity gain — verified via Audio Precision APx555 bench testing. Unlike most overdrives that compress early or color aggressively, the ICE 9 preserves pick attack, string separation, and harmonic integrity across its entire gain range (0–10), while offering two distinct voicings: 'Classic' (a warm, asymmetric clipping profile inspired by vintage Vox AC30 preamp stages) and 'Modern' (a tighter, symmetrical clipping mode with extended low-end response and enhanced high-frequency clarity). Measured input impedance sits at 1.2 MΩ, output impedance at 680 Ω, and current draw at a modest 12 mA — making it compatible with standard 9 V DC power supplies and true-bypass loopers. This review documents hands-on testing across six guitar/amp combinations, spectral analysis, and direct comparisons against the Ibanez Tube Screamer TS9, Wampler Ego Compressor + Plexi Drive stack, and the Fulltone OCD v2.5. Engineering Philosophy and Circuit Architecture Vox’s design team — led by senior engineer Dr. Hiroshi Tanaka (formerly of Roland R&D) — approached the ICE 9 as a departure from conventional op-amp-based overdrive topologies. Instead, they opted for a fully discrete, Class-A biased JFET signal path, using hand-matched Toshiba 2SK370 N-channel and 2SJ109 P-channel transistors in a complementary pair configuration. This architecture avoids the phase inversion artifacts common in single-JFET designs and enables true symmetrical clipping in Modern mode without sacrificing transient fidelity. Each unit undergoes DC bias calibration at the factory, ensuring gate-source voltages remain within ±3 mV tolerance across the production run — a spec confirmed during teardown verification of three randomly selected retail units. The pedal features a hybrid gain structure: the first stage provides clean buffer amplification (up to +25 dB), while the second stage introduces voltage-controlled overdrive via a dual-clipping diode array (1N5819 Schottky diodes for fast recovery and soft saturation, paired with red LED-based clipping in Classic mode for gentle compression). A unique feature is the 'Dynamic Response Switch' — a miniature DPDT toggle located beneath the footswitch — which alters the feedback network’s time constant, shifting the effective slew rate from 4.2 V/µs (Classic) to 12.7 V/µs (Modern). This directly impacts how the pedal reacts to picking dynamics: Classic mode exhibits subtle sag and bloom on sustained notes; Modern mode delivers near-instantaneous transient capture with minimal overshoot. Power Supply and Thermal Management Unlike many boutique pedals that rely solely on linear regulators, the ICE 9 integrates a TI TPS7A47 ultra-low-noise LDO (with 4.17 µV RMS noise floor) followed by a discrete RC filtering stage. Internal thermal imaging (performed using FLIR E6 thermal camera) shows maximum junction temperature rise of just 8.3°C after 90 minutes of continuous operation at full gain — well below the 30°C safety margin required for long-term reliability. The PCB uses 2-oz copper layers and thermally anchored ground planes beneath all active components, contributing to consistent performance across ambient temperatures from −10°C to +45°C. online Documents SPECS Specs PHOTOS Photos Product Description Iconic amp sounds for your pedalboard. The Silk Drive valve overdrive pedal offers the dynamic clean and creamy overdrive tones of classic boutique amps in a compact pedal format, powered by Nutube for warm and responsive amp-like tones. Inspired by harmonically rich boutique amp tones, the Silk Drive goes beyond the amp-in-a-box category to offer a truly flexible valve overdrive pedal. The all-analog signal path and Nutube allow for genuine boost and overdrive tones with the feel of a real tube amp, while internally boosted voltage gives greater headroom and dynamics. Plus, the OLED display shows an oscilloscope while the pedal is active or bypassed, allowing you to understand exactly how your signal is affected. Three output modes allow you to use this as a standard pedal, a line-level preamp, and a direct amp-sim using the built-in analog cabinet simulator. Use STANDARD mode with your normal guitar rig to totally transform your amp, or use PREAMP or CAB-SIM mode while recording directly into your audio interface. In each mode, the all-analog design and active EQ allow you to perfectly dial in the sound you need in any situation. The Channel Link feature allows you to chain two or more Valvenergy pedals together, through the Link jack of each pedal. Using a with a standard 1/8” stereo cable will link 2 pedals, and using a stereo 1/8” splitter will link 3 or 4 pedals. This allows you to turn one pedal on while bypassing the others, as if you were switching between channels of a guitar amp. These pedals are equipped with a high-contrast OLED display showing an oscilloscope, a visual indication of how the waveform is affected by the knob settings. This display allows shows which mode you are currently using. Classic mid-humped breakup with true bypass switching. The V810 Valvetone was introduced in 1998 as Vox's take on the classic Tube Screamer circuit. Volume, Tone, and Gain controls provide moderate gain range from subtle to medium overdrive while preserving dynamics. The circuit uses a Texas Instruments RC4558P op-amp with 'millennium bypass' and stabilized power section. Unlike many budget Tube Screamer variants, the V810 features true bypass switching for signal purity when disengaged. The die-cast aluminum case with chrome bezel and embossed diamond-pattern tread matches classic Vox aesthetics. 9V battery powered. Originally $120, the V810 was considered expensive but is now valued for its build quality and responsive, classic overdrive tone. Out of stock Add to Wishlist SKU: v810 Categories: Effects , General , Pedals , Pre-Owned Effects , Pre-Owned Pedals Description Vox introduced two new guitar effects pedals in the summer of 1998. Similar to a “tube screamer,” the Vox V810 “Valvetone” pedal was designed to simulate the tone of an overdriven guitar amplifier. Vox also introduced the V830 “Distortion Booster.” As in the 1960s, “Distortion Booster” was Vox parlance for fuzz tone. The V810 Valvetone and the V830 Distortion Booster pedals were included in the 1998-1999 Vox catalog , 1999-2000 Vox catalog , and a single page sales flyer . Unlike the relatively simple V829 Vox Tone Bender circuit that required only ten electronic components, the parts list for the Valvetone and Distortion Booster pedals included a total of about three dozen resistors, capacitors, and semiconductors. Two “old school” germanium transistors powered the V829 Tone Bender circuit. The Valvetone and Distortion Booster pedals used a modern Texas Instruments RC4558P integrated circuit opamp to add gain to the input signal. Like the Vox wah, the die cast aluminum case for the V810 and V830 was painted black and topped with a chrome plated bezel and a rubber tread. The tread featured an embosssed Vox diamond pattern. Each pedal included three controls. The V810 Valvetone featured a Volume, Tone and a Gain control. The V830 Distortion Booster offered a Volume, Tone and a Drive control. Drive adjusted the intensity of the fuzz. A nine volt battery powered the pedal. The V830 Distortion Booster replaced the V829 Tone Bender that Vox offered from 1994-1997. Country of Origin, Vox V810 Valve-Tone and V830 Vox Distortion Booster Pedals: China. Even though the Gibson Maestro Fuzz Tone featured in the Rolling Stones 1965 hit (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction had been introduced in 1962, the effect pedal had previously gained little traction in the marketplace. The chart success of "Satisfaction" convinced every guitarist that they needed a fuzz tone. Various manufacturers in the US and UK tooled up to produce them. Gary Hurst, a UK based amplifier tech, started to produce and market fuzz tones in 1965. One of his early accounts was the Musical Exchange in London. Hurst soon teamed with the Musical Exchange to produce pedals under the Sola Sound brand. Anxious to enter the fuzz tone market, JMI entered into an agreement with the Musical Exchange to purchase Sola Sound fuzz pedals rebranded with the Vox "Tone Bender" name. A 1968 purchase order from JMI to the Musical Exchange for Tone Benders can be seen below. Thomas Organ, the American distributor of Vox, chose to bypass Sola Sound. Thomas Organ had a close relationship with the Italian manufacturer JEN. The V828 Vox Tone Bender and many Vox organs for the US market were produced by JEN. The two pedals shown on the top of this page are examples of the Thomas V828 Tone Bender produced by JEN. Some of these pedals were finished in black "crinkle coat" paint while others were adorned with gray hammertone. The Sola Sound Tone Bender had a sand cast aluminum case. The JEN case was die cast aluminum. A steel base covered the bottom of the pedal. The pedal was powered by a 9V battery clipped to the inside bottom of the base. The Tone Bender circuit was similar to the input stage of the Vox T.60 amplifier head. The JEN Tone Bender circuit included an SFT363 and an SFT337 germanium transistor, two capacitors and six resistors. The Sola Tone Bender circuit was similar but substituted a pair of OC76 germanium transistors for the SFT363 and SFT337. One rotary control adjusted output level, a second adjusted the "attack" or intensity of the fuzz. No use on online auctions, eBay or Reverb. The Vox V829 Tone Bender "Fuzz" was one of first products introduced under the Korg ownership of the Vox brand. It was included in the 1994, 1995, 1996 and 1997 Vox price lists and featured in a 1994 sales flyer . The V829 was based on the circuitry of the V828 Tone Bender that was produced during the Thomas Organ ownership period of Vox (1965 - 1971). The V828 Tone Bender was manufactured for Thomas Organ by the Italian manufacturer JEN. The JMI version of the Tone Bender was produced by Sola Sound of London. The circuitry for both the V828 and V829 Tone Benders utilized two PNP germanium transistors. Sola installed a pair of European OC76 V828 Tone Bender transistors into the UK model. JEN installed an SFT363 and an SFT337 transistor into the version of the V828 Tone Bender sold in the North American market place. The Thomas Organ V828 service manual indicated that if European specification transistors were not available, a pair of SK3004 germanium transistors would be a suitable field replacement. The Korg/Vox V829 Tone Bender used a pair of these SK3004 germanium transistors. 3_Footer Contents • UK Vox Amplifiers • US Vox Amplifiers • Vox Organs • Vox Guitars Vox Effects • My 1960's Vox Band • What's New • Search the Vox Showroom US Vox Schematics • UK Vox Schematics • Vox Catalogs • Owners Manuals Photos and editorial content courtesy Gary Hahlbeck Any and all material presented herein is protected by Copyright. © 1998 - 2026 The Vox Showroom, all rights reserved The images and editorial content in this web site may not be copied or reproduced in online auction sites such as eBay, Reverb and Craig's List. The trapezoidal shape of the die cast aluminum case allowed several Vox 7000 series to form a curved array on the floor. But rumor has it that someone is smuggling fuzz — the most-coveted contraband — back into circulation. The Contraband is a single-knob fuzz machine that ravages your guitar signal and generates a metallic wall of sound. Because of its size, it’s easy to smuggle into regions where fuzz is not welcome. The Contraband packs a huge punch for being in a petite enclosure. The single volume knob lets you decide how loud your signal will be, while the tone switch can help thin out humbuckers or beef up single-coils. The natural bass frequencies of different guitars and pickup combinations, at times can be too much; this is where the Thick and Thin switch comes in handy. Single-coil pickups may sound better in Thick mode, while humbuckers may sound better in Thin mode, but you can find versatile and complimentary tones in both positions no matter the pickup selection. The mild built-in gate allows you to get those choked-off, dying-battery sounds when you roll down your guitar’s volume knob. sources.title: Walrus Audio Iron Horse LM308 Distortion — Ground Floor Guitar
sources.description: The Iron Horse is Walrus’s take on a classic distortion circuit that’s thick, punchy, riffy, and rowdy. With the help of the Si/LED (Silicon/LED) knob and wide range of the distortion knob, this true bypass, high-gain behemoth can be finely tuned for clear overdriven sounds or let the reigns loose for a full-on distorted onslaught. nbsp; Top mount jacks with soft switch bypassing and art by David Hüttner complete the package for a pedal board-ready distortion machine. nbsp; The Iron Horse nbsp;V3 updates are as follows: Top-mounted jacks Soft relay true bypass on/off Fixed volume drop-off when the distortion knob is at minimum Re-imagined the hard clipping toggle as a blend style potentiometer, that allows you to blend between symmetrical silicon and diode clipping for a new variety of tones. Owners of the previous versions of the Iron Horse will be familiar with the three distortion modes operated by a toggle switch to change between different clipping modes. The switch has now been replaced with a blending knob opening up a wealth of ways to alter your tone. When the knob is set to the left, the distorted signal will be using Silicon clipping diodes adding in a high amount of compression. Rotating the knob to the right will bring in LED clipping and a smaller amount of compression. Putting the knob at noon will blend between the two using different ratios of the Silicone and LED clipping diodes for more complex clipping sounds. Note: Since the Si/LED knob is changing the internal gain and clipping style, the other controls will behave slightly differently as well. You will need to use the volume knob to adjust the overall output up or down depending on where you have the knob set.

Walrus Audio Kangra Filter Fuzz quantity Add to cart SKU: GEMWF798452 Category: Fuzz 84 people are viewing this right now Estimated Delivery: Sep 30 - Oct 5 Free Shipping & Returns: On all orders Description Description From Walrus: Would you like to command all of existence with the authority of one guitar strike? The Kangra Filter Fuzz is a true bypass, two-in-one pedal that provides a thick and spatty octave fuzz, and a psychedelic filter thats great for sweeps, frequency boost or even envelope filter sounds. The filter can run independently, or with the fuzz feeding into it. This is no rhythm player’s fuzz. Dig in and play dirty with aggressive fuzz lead lines that’ll rip time and space apart at the seams. SNL Guitarist and fuzz fanatic, Jared Scharff, approached us about doing a modern filtered and fuzz inspired by his favorite vintage fuzz pedal, the Kay Fuzz Tone. Working together through hundreds of texts, calls, emails and mailing prototypes back and forth, the Kangra came to life with plenty of grit, teeth and vintage vibe, as well as pronounced modern features. FUZZ Get two different styles of fuzz with the M/V Switch. In the modern position (M), you notice a more forgiving fuzz with longer and tighter sustain, while the Vintage position (V) feels starved with spatty breakup and grittier, shorter sustain. FILTER The Kangra also has a versatile filter with Resonance, Sensitivity, Frequency and Envelope Filter controls. Use the filter on its own to add a unique shape to your sound, or flip the Envelope Filter switch and open up funky sixties style tones. “On the filter, I wanted to go for that vintage mpc 3000 low pass type of thing…Or similar to doing a low pass plug-in for a track, or like a dj would do without it being too “wah pedal” like, and this achieved that.” – Jared Scharff The art was inspired by a once in a life time expedition Jared took to the Kangra Valley near the Himalaya Mountains. It was there his journey inspired new ideas that can only approximated by the Kangra Filter Fuzz. The pedal comes in a peach enclosure with art by Adam Forster in white and blue inks. They have been harnessed and woven together for an eternity of ethereal power with The Melee: Wall of Noise. The Melee unapologetically uses a joystick to meld reverb and distortion into one massive blaze of sound. With the flip of the order switch, run the distortion into the reverb or reverb into distortion; signal chain is your call now. For the explorer, the Melee can run one of three different reverb programs Ambient, Octave, and Reverse. In a less is more approach, they’ve intentionally decided on controls that are fun to use and will inspire a wealth of creative output. Use the joystick to control the amount of distortion by moving it up and down. Moving the joystick left and right will adjust your reverb mix. The tone and decay toggles have low, medium, and high settings. Modulation can be added to the wet signal by holding down the bypass switch and moving the decay toggle. The left position is no modulation, the middle is a slight modulation, and the right is a high modulation. ALGORITHMS The Melee is equipped with three different reverb programs, which can be changed by simultaneously pressing the bypass and sustain stomp switches. Experiment with the order toggle switch to hear how differently these all react in front and after the distortion! • Ambient Reverb (Pink LED) - Huge reverb capable of massive trails and engulfing your chords into an angry wash of sound. Great for soaring melodic lines or shoegaze-driven chord progressions. • Octave Down Reverb (Yellow LED) - Similar to the Dark mode in the Slö, you’ll find an eerie lower octave hovering in the reverb trail for a nice and dark atmospheric touch. • Reverse Reverb with Feedback (Blue LED) - Add reversed reverb trails back into your signal, create gentle melodies or push into reverse feedback overload. Big, slow, and sad chords love to hang out here. MOMENTARY Press and hold the sustain switch to ramp up the reverb trails. Release and the trails will ramp back down to where the decay switch is currently set. The sustain switch can also latch in all three programs. From its lowest to highest settings, the Voyager provides a uniquely superb amount of clarity to any style of playing. sources.description: There was something almost magical about certain amplifiers from the 1960’s. Wampler’s Black ‘65 pedal captures the tonal nuances and rich harmonics associated with this classic era!

sources.bodyExcerpt: Black ’65 Limited Edition | Wampler Pedals Home Shop All Pedals Distortion / Overdrive Compression Fuzz Delay / Reverb Modulation Boost Utilities Discontinued Plugins Merchandise Dealers Community Blog Artists Podcast Videos Support About Downloads FAQs Warranty Registration Withdrawal Request Contact Us search account_circle My Account search Products search Black ’65 Limited Edition There was something almost magical about certain amplifiers from the 1960’s. Wampler’s Black ‘65 pedal captures the tonal nuances and rich harmonics associated with this classic era! Out of stock Watch video Overview Features Videos Technical Downloads Out of stock “While the world moves increasingly toward digital modeling, these analog circuits offer something uniquely compelling.” Right facing | Front | Left facing | Back | Top |' data-navmenu="off" data-hashurl="off" data-menuSlider="off" data-continue-autoplay="off" data-outside-nav="off" data-autoplay="off" > 4 5 There was something magical about certain amps from the 1960s, amps that have become to be known as the "blackface" or "black panel" style of amplifiers from a certain legendary American guitar and amplifier company. With such a rich legacy of tone to follow, Grand Pappy BDub’s take on the American-voiced amps of that period was turned into the legendary Black ‘65 Pedal. Through a clean amp, this pedal offers a faithful reproduction of the tones Brian loved from this classic period, and it is also flexible enough to add a new level of nuanced grit to your existing rig. This is a limited edition pedal and only available to purchase online here from Wamplerpedals.com. Once they’re gone, they’re gone! $ 199.97 Out of stock SKU: WMP-B65-PED Category: Distortion / Overdrive Tags: AIAB , Amp , Black 65 warning Cancer and Reproductive Harm www.p65warnings.ca.gov Limited Edition, Classic Tones Although the Black ’65 delivers the sound of those vintage tones you have come to love and expect, it is not limited to only one particular sound. With a 3 band eq similar to a vintage ”black panel” amp, you’re able to sculpt the tonality, feel, compression and overall gain structure just like you would on the real tube amplifier it’s emulating. Get Boosted The Boost switch controls the amount of internal gain available to the pedal – handy when dealing with different guitar output levels or just as some extra grunt to push this into primitive breakup – very similar to high levels of rectification that became the trademark tonal quality of a famous Californian boutique amp manufacturer. Vintage Playability This pedal sounds great with every type of pickup we’ve thrown at it. Whether you are slinging a single coil, looking for that classic Nashville twang, or driving a Humbucker into a 4×12, this pedal will take your tone back to an era that defined the history of music and beyond. Amp in a Pedal This is one of Wampler’s legendary circuits reborn in a limited edition pedal that works great with any amplifier or even direct into your favorite cabinet sim or IR loader. Hear it in action: Technical Details Limited Edition Built in the U.S.A. High-grade components selected for superior sound and response Controls: Volume, Gain, Bass, Middle and Treble, Boost Switch Boost Switch toggles between lower and higher gain mode. Battery connection and 9V power jack This pedal draws approximately 3mA at 9V and 9mA at 18V. 2.5″ x 4.5″ x 1.5″ in size (63.5mm x 114.3mm x 38.1mm) – height excludes knobs and switches Black panel magic There was something almost magical about the “black panel” amplifiers of the 1960’s… Out of stock 5 Year Limited Warranty Each Wampler product that bears the official “Wampler – Built in USA” logo is custom designed and assembled in the USA using premium globally sourced components chosen for superior sound and response. sources.bodyExcerpt: Wampler Pedals Unveils the Catapulp OD Distortion and Tumnus OD Boost: Dual-Channel Overdrive Innovation Meets Studio-Grade Circuit Refinement | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Wampler Pedals Unveils the Catapulp OD Distortion and Tumnus OD Boost: Dual-Channel Overdrive Innovation Meets Studio-Grade Circuit Refinement By Liam Carter July 13, 2026 Two New Overdrives, One Unified Vision Wampler Pedals has officially launched the Catapulp OD Distortion and Tumnus OD Boost—two distinct yet complementary overdrive pedals designed to address nuanced tonal demands across modern guitar rigs. Announced on March 12, 2024, at the NAMM Show in Anaheim, both units ship with Wampler’s signature powder-coated aluminum enclosures, LED-lit footswitches with status indicators, and internal voltage regulation ensuring consistent performance from 9V to 18V DC. Unlike many boutique manufacturers releasing single-unit updates, Wampler intentionally developed these pedals as a coordinated pair: the Catapulp targets players seeking saturated, harmonically rich distortion with dynamic touch sensitivity, while the Tumnus OD Boost serves as a transparent, articulate boost/overdrive optimized for pedalboard stacking and amp interaction. Both units measure 4.5" × 3.75" × 1.75" and weigh 1.2 lbs—identical dimensions enabling seamless integration into existing pedalboards without footprint compromise. Engineering Philosophy: Beyond Clipping Diodes Wampler’s design team, led by co-founder Brian Wampler and lead engineer Chris Doss, spent 14 months refining analog signal paths that prioritize harmonic integrity over brute-force saturation. Rather than relying solely on silicon or germanium diode clipping, both pedals implement hybrid clipping topologies. The Catapulp uses a cascaded dual-stage architecture: the first stage employs asymmetrical MOSFET-based clipping (IRF510 transistor pair), followed by a second stage using matched 1N5817 Schottky diodes biased at ±0.62V for low-forward-voltage soft clipping. This configuration produces a 22.3dB gain increase at maximum Drive (measured at 1kHz, unity input level) while retaining note definition even at high saturation settings. In contrast, the Tumnus OD Boost utilizes a modified JFET-input buffer stage feeding into a discrete op-amp circuit (Texas Instruments OPA2134PA) before hitting a dynamically biased 1N4148 diode pair—engineered to clip only when transient peaks exceed 1.2Vpp, preserving clean headroom until intentional drive is applied. Power & Signal Integrity Both pedals feature Wampler’s proprietary Clean Power Regulation System (CPRS), which maintains ±0.05V stability across the 9–18V input range. Internal DC-DC conversion isolates the analog path from ripple noise, resulting in measured noise floors of ≤−87.2dBV (A-weighted) at unity gain—verified using Audio Precision APx555 test equipment. Independent bench testing confirmed no measurable difference in THD+N (Total Harmonic Distortion plus Noise) between 9V and 18V operation: 0.08% at 1kHz, 0dBu input, for both units. This eliminates the common 'more voltage = more output' myth; instead, higher voltages expand dynamic headroom and transient response without altering core voicing. The Catapulp OD Distortion: Saturated Texture with Surgical Control The Catapulp OD Distortion distinguishes itself through three dedicated controls—Drive, Tone, and Volume—and an innovative Voice toggle switch offering two distinct clipping voicings. In ‘Vintage’ mode, the circuit emphasizes midrange warmth (peaking at 720Hz ±15Hz) with subtle compression and a smooth high-end roll-off beginning at 5.1kHz. In ‘Modern’ mode, the clipping network shifts bias points to deliver tighter low-end response (−1.8dB at 85Hz), extended treble presence (+2.3dB at 8.4kHz), and 38% faster attack envelope (measured via 10–90% rise time: 1.7ms vs. 2.7ms in Vintage). You get the Dracarys. This vicious stompbox effortlessly embraces any sub-genre of metal, thanks to its finely tuned EQ and Tight/Open switch. But tap into its decidedly modern soul, and the Dracarys will instantly morph your clean amp into one of the most savage and modern high-gain powerhouses this side of Mr. Englund himself. As Ola puts it, no matter type of high-gain tones you’re looking for, “It can definitely deliver the chug.” Brian Wampler’s ability to distill the playing experience of a cranked guitar amp into a box that fits on your pedalboard makes him among the premier effects builders in the world. So when he came across the genre-defining tones on Ola Englund’s YouTube channel, the gauntlet was thrown down. He had to create a pedal that contained that same searing gain, percussive low end, unparalleled note clarity. He had to create the Dracarys. There are almost as many legendary heavy metal guitar tones as there are headbangers, and the Dracarys nails each those tones admirably. It’s not about the gain, well… not completely, it’s about the voicing, the depth, the agression and most importantly, the power. The Dracarys melts faces, but only on your command. You need a classic rock OD, drop that gain down and be amazed at what you hear! Fire breather The complexity of the gain in the Dracarys is what makes it so powerful, it’s not a thick blanket like other pedals, it’s not a fuzz style, it’s the clearest, heaviest and most crushing gain you’ll ever hear… it’s almost enough gain to grant you Swedish residency. Watch video Out of stock Overview Features Videos Technical Downloads Out of stock “The Germanium Tumnus is our tribute to classic pedal designs, but with a unique twist.” Right facing | Front | Left facing | Back | Top |' data-navmenu="off" data-hashurl="off" data-menuSlider="off" data-continue-autoplay="off" data-outside-nav="off" data-autoplay="off" > 4 5 SOLD OUT There is one overdrive circuit to this day that has been among the most talked about, the most sought after, and the most mythical of them all. It‘s that legendary tone that every guitarist dreams of. Brian Wampler captured that magic with his original Tumnus circuit, and it has since graced the pedalboards of thousands of players around the world. The Tumnus has withstood the test of time and held its own in countless pedal shootouts, often coming out on top even against the original Klon pedal. The allure of that original overdrive had a lot to do with a very specific “secret” germanium diode, dubbed “unobtanium” by the original creator, Bill Finnegan. It was said that these diodes were the heartbeat of the coveted tone, but they had run out long ago. Despite this Wampler fans have been asking Brian to create a Tumnus using the same vintage specification clipping diode from those early Klons. After a massive hunt Brian found a small stash of these elusive diodes and used them to create a limited-edition run of pedals - the Germanium Tumnus. The Germanium Tumnus is a versatile addition to any pedal board. Stack it with another pedal to help push or shape the total amount of gain, use it as a slightly dirty boost to push the front end of your amp over the edge, or use it as a standalone overdrive pedal and let it roar as nature intended. $ 179.97 Out of stock SKU: WMP-TGE-PED-SIL Categories: Boost Utilities , Distortion / Overdrive Tags: boost , overdrive warning Cancer and Reproductive Harm www.p65warnings.ca.gov A Twist on a Classic There is a reason the Tumnus has gained the reputation it has – it provides the perfect high headroom overdrive to send your tone into the place you’ve always dreamed it would go. The Germanium Tumnus adds an extra dimension with Germanium clipping diodes that help give this circuit some extra sizzle. This pedal will satisfy both the pedal connoisseur and those seeking a new workhorse on their board. Always the Right Fit If you want a pre-gain boost to fatten up your tone… the Germanium Tumnus delivers. If you want a standalone overdrive…. the Germanium Tumnus delivers. If you want…well, you get the picture here. Set the gain around 9 o’clock for a beautiful smooth boost and at noon for a fuller voiced, meaty drive. Turn the gain all the way up for a brutal, yet creamy overdriven tone. The Germanium Tumnus, like its golden sibling, delivers. Brian’s Special Stash After a massive hunt Brian sourced a quantity of vintage specification Germanium diodes and used them to create this limited-edition run of pedals – the Germanium Tumnus was born. This edition is steeped in a level of exclusivity with a tone that’s set to become legendary. This stash of “secret diodes” is limited, giving you a rare opportunity to own a piece of tone shaping history. Once they’re gone, they’re gone and this pedal will be discontinued. It's a Tumnus, it’s a deluxe, and it's loaded with the same style of hyper-rare germanium diodes as the elusive Klon Centaur and the sold-out Germanium Tumnus. This is my shot at the ultimate Klon-style overdrive. You all sure love the Germanium Tumnus! It was almost sold out before it even shipped. Never fear if you missed your chance to get one, though. The Ltd. Germanium Tumnus Deluxe is the quintessential blend of that same authentic tone and added versatility. With a 3-band EQ, buffer bypass switch, controls for level and gain, and a hot switch for increased gain, you can think of it as an upgraded Germanium Tumnus, an even more versatile Klon, or a killer overdrive/boost pedal in its own right. However you see it—or use it—you'll love it. I only had so many of these "magic" diodes, so, like the first Germanium Tumnus, production is extremely limited. Assuming you haven't bought them up already, you'll want to act fast. When they're gone, they're gone. Limited Edition, You Know the Drill! I only have a limited supply of those vintage diodes, so this pedal won't be around long. If you're curious, move quick. You won't regret it. $ 309.97 Out of stock SKU: WMP-TDG-PED Categories: Boost Utilities , Distortion / Overdrive Tags: boost , overdrive warning Cancer and Reproductive Harm www.p65warnings.ca.gov Legendary Diodes, Iconic Tone There are so many Klones out there that it’s hard to keep up. That’s just fine with me. My original Tumnus is still a favorite of guitarists around the world. That said, they’re nearly all missing the unique germanium diodes that powered Bill Finnegan’s classic design. Not so with the Germanium Tumnus Deluxe. I found an exceedingly rare stash of germanium diodes electronically identical to the ones Finnegan used. Thanks to them, the Germanium Tumnus Deluxe is as close as you can get to his ’90s icons. That Tone With Any Rig, Every Time The Germanium Tumnus Deluxe and the sold-out Germanium Tumnus are essentially the same circuits. The Deluxe’s 3-band EQ just gives you finer control without losing the pedal’s inherent character. Want to add a bit of low-end back into the mix? Need some extra cut and attack? How about boosting a crunchy amp with a tighter, more percussive sound? It’s all there, and it’s all authentic. More Gain With the Flip of a Switch The Germanium Tumnus Deluxe also features my “hot switch,” which introduces more output and drive than most Klones. That includes my my OG Tumnus. This style of pedal is already a quintessential clean boost and mid-gain overdrive. Now, it has a meaner side while retaining the classic vocal-like tone and throaty response you expect. To Buffer or Not to Buffer This style of overdrive pedal gives your tone more clarity and character. It’s often used as an always-on tonal sweetener but still adds some magic when bypassed. sources.title: Brent Mason: Hot Wired v2 | Wampler Pedals
sources.description: Two pedals in one (overdrive and distortion), the Hot Wired is without doubt one of the most versatile pedals available today. One channel of the Hot Wired has all your overdrive needs, from a gentle break up to all out crunch, the other gives you dirt… Loads of fat, creamy distortion that is tonally perfect from top to bottom. If need be you can stack them both together for a huge, huge sound.

sources.bodyExcerpt: Brent Mason: Hot Wired v2 | Wampler Pedals Home Shop All Pedals Distortion / Overdrive Compression Fuzz Delay / Reverb Modulation Boost Utilities Discontinued Plugins Merchandise Dealers Community Blog Artists Podcast Videos Support About Downloads FAQs Warranty Registration Withdrawal Request Contact Us search account_circle My Account search Products search DISCONTINUED Brent Mason: Hot Wired v2 The Brent Mason Hot Wired v2. The only pedal versatile enough to be taken into the world’s most demanding studio environment every day… Nashville master sessions. Out of stock Watch video Overview Features Videos Technical Downloads Out of stock Front | Left facing | Back | Right facing | Top |' data-navmenu="off" data-hashurl="off" data-menuSlider="off" data-continue-autoplay="off" data-outside-nav="off" data-autoplay="off" > 4 5 A lot of people think they’ve never heard of Brent Mason. We would bet that although they may not recognize the name, chances are huge that they have heard him. Brent is, without doubt, the number 1 session guitarist working out of Nashville and has been since the early 1990’s. Not only is he a legendary studio figure, but also a renowned composer and songwriter. His compositions have been used in countless films, TV shows and commercials. His solo albums, in particular “Hot Wired” (from which this pedal got its name) has become almost mythical in its reputation for guitar tone and quality of musicianship. With Brent, you will not believe it until you hear it. Built on the foundations of the extremely popular v1, v2 stands alone in terms of versatility. The studio scene in Nashville has changed over the last few years, so we changed the Hot Wired to mirror the industry Brent works in. v1 was geared towards all out chickin’ pickin’ and beyond. sources.bodyExcerpt: Wampler Pedals Brent Mason Hot Wired V2 Review: In-Depth Tone Analysis | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Wampler Pedals Brent Mason Hot Wired V2 Review: In-Depth Tone Analysis By zoe-langford June 20, 2026 Wampler Pedals Brent Mason Hot Wired V2 Review The Wampler Brent Mason Hot Wired V2 is a transparent, low-to-medium gain overdrive pedal engineered for dynamic response, touch sensitivity, and studio-grade clarity—ideal for country, blues, rock, and clean-boost applications where articulation matters more than saturation. It delivers consistent headroom, minimal compression, and a natural midrange lift that complements single-coil and humbucker pickups without masking their character. This Wampler Pedals Brent Mason Hot Wired V2 pedal review confirms it excels in nuanced playing scenarios—especially for players who prioritize note separation, pick attack fidelity, and seamless integration with amp-driven overdrive—but falls short if you seek high-gain distortion or aggressive clipping textures. Its $249 price reflects premium construction and voicing precision, not feature overload. About Wampler Pedals Brent Mason Hot Wired V2 Wampler Pedals, founded in 2007 by Brian Wampler in Nashville, Tennessee, built its reputation on hand-wired, analog overdrives and boosts designed with professional session musicians in mind. The original Hot Wired debuted in 2012 as a collaboration with legendary session guitarist Brent Mason—a player known for his articulate Telecaster work on hundreds of country hits and his preference for pedals that enhance rather than replace amp tone. The V2 revision arrived in late 2020 after extensive user feedback and internal R D aimed at refining dynamics, tightening bass response, and improving noise floor consistency across gain settings 1 . Unlike many signature pedals that merely slap a name on a generic circuit, this one underwent iterative voicing sessions with Mason himself, focusing on preserving transient response while adding subtle harmonic complexity only when demanded by playing intensity. First Impressions Unboxing reveals a compact, rugged enclosure (4.75" × 2.75" × 1.75") with a matte black powder-coated aluminum chassis and bold white silkscreen labeling. The footswitch is a heavy-duty, soft-click, true-bypass momentary switch with tactile feedback—no spring fatigue or wobble. All knobs are CTS 25k audio-taper pots with rubberized knurls for grip, even with damp fingers. The LED is bright but non-distracting (amber when engaged), and the input/output jacks are recessed Neutrik units mounted directly to the chassis—not PCB-mounted—reducing strain on solder joints. A subtle but effective detail: the battery door uses a stainless steel screw instead of plastic, and the internal battery clip has gold-plated contacts. No sticker residue, no misaligned silkscreening—build quality immediately signals attention to long-term reliability. Detailed Specifications The Hot Wired V2 employs discrete JFET-based circuitry (not op-amp reliant) with a Class-A biased front-end stage and passive tone shaping. Its architecture avoids clipping diodes in the signal path—instead relying on JFET saturation and cascaded gain stages for organic breakup. Key specs: Circuit Type: Discrete JFET, Class-A biased, diode-free overdrive Power Requirements: 9–18V DC center-negative (regulated), 50mA draw; no battery option (V2 removed 9V battery support) Controls: Drive (0–10), Volume (0–10), Tone (0–10), Presence (0–10) True Bypass: Yes, relay-based switching with status LED Input Impedance: 1.2MΩ (optimized for passive pickups) Output Impedance: 500Ω (low-Z, compatible with buffered loops) THD @ 1kHz: <0.3% at unity gain, <1.8% at max Drive The absence of battery power isn’t a limitation—it’s an engineering choice. In stock Mofetta quantity Add to cart Watch video Overview Features Videos Technical Downloads In stock Mofetta quantity Add to cart “A Modern Twist on the ‘Mostortion’ Pedal Circuitry” Right facing | Front | Left facing | Back | Top |' data-navmenu="off" data-hashurl="off" data-menuSlider="off" data-continue-autoplay="off" data-outside-nav="off" data-autoplay="off" > 4 5 The Wampler Mofetta Overdrive/Distortion is my tribute to the MOSFET-driven magic of a 1990s classic — the MT10 MOSTORTION tm . A mainstay of countless top session players, the Mofetta honors the soul of that elusive yet classic circuit while revealing its untapped potential. Think of the Mofetta as a supercharged MOSTORTION tm , reborn and amplified. I made sure that it delivered the classic, amp-like overdrive, massive headroom, and versatile 3-band EQ that made the original so famous. But I also wanted more and added a Texture Switch that introduces actual MOSFETs into the pedal's overdrive section for a bolder, more articulate tone. The Mofetta preserves everything you love about the early '90s legend with a powerful new dimension. The original MT10 MOSTORTION tm was released in 1990 as part of a budget pedal series to meet the demand of a growing market. Despite the pedal's "cheaper" qualities, guitarists began to take note of its amp-like low-gain tones, attributing them—arguably incorrectly—to the onboard MOSFET Op-amps. Though the pedals were discontinued a couple of years later, used ones command insane prices today and are extremely hard to find. The Mofetta is my way of bringing it all back and re-creating those singing tones while diving even further into the amp-like world of MOSFETs. But like its predecessor, it’s the circuit’s low-to-mid-gain voice that the original circuit is most known for. From edge-of-breakup to fat, vintage amp-style crunch, the Mofetta blooms with tube-like compression, always retaining its musical warmth. And with its high-headroom output, it easily pushes your amp or modeler into harmonically-rich breakup. 3-band EQ Part of what makes the Mofetta so versatile is its unique 3-band EQ. While many overdrives before 1990 relied on a simple tone knob, the idea of a dirt pedal like the MOSTORTION tm with bass, middle, and treble controls was darn near revolutionary. It lets you dial in the Mofetta for a full-range drive or achieve transparent grit that complements your clean tone. If you dial up the mids and treble a bit, you can even use it as a focused boost to push your amp’s breakup, or stacking with another gain pedal, tightening its response and enhancing its character. True MOSFET Clipping One of the original MOSTORTION’s tm little known “secrets” is that it doesn’t actually use MOSFETs for its overdrive. It uses a “MOSFET based op-amp”, but it uses clipping diodes to produce distortion. IndyGuitarist Wampler Pedals browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by enclosure pedal Wampler Pedals PlexTortion Published on November 2, 2007 Wampler Pedals distortion pedal Information Wampler Pedals The Plextortion is a distortion pedal that was originally designed to emulate a JCM800 with celestion greenbacks (Back in Black era AC/DC tones through van halen, dokken, ratt, and all those amazing 80's rock "cranked Marshall" tones). It has a very 'brown' sounding distortion, a bit similar to the pinnacle pedal. It differs from the pinnacle in that it is a tighter distortion, more like preamp tube distortion where the pinnacle is a bit looser, more like power tube distortion. The Super Plextortion differs from the standard Plextortion in that it has 3 totally different gain structures. It is more of a transparent type of tone (more of a celestion vintage 30 type of tone) where the standard plextortion has more of a mid focused marshally 'greenback' sound to it. Basically, the super plextortion is more of a modern sounding distortion where the standard plextortion is more vintage sounding. I've noticed that some guys like play their distortion pedals that emulate marshall tones THROUGH a marshall. Let's be honest - I can play a chorus pedal through a marshall and get a very "marshally" sounding chorus pedal... In my opinion this isn't a fair or accurate representation of a pedal. Because of this, I record my clips and videos through everyday affordable guitars and amps in order to be as accurate as possible. sources.description: A detailed, hands-on comparison of Wampler’s Super Plextortion and Pinnacle overdrive/distortion pedals — covering circuit design, tonal character, gain staging, noise floor, build quality, and real-world performance with Stratocasters, Les Pauls, and various amps including Marshall JCM800, Fender Twin Reverb, and Friedman BE-100.

sources.bodyExcerpt: Wampler Pedals Super Plextortion and Pinnacle Review: Dual High-Gain Powerhouses Tested Side-by-Side | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Wampler Pedals Super Plextortion and Pinnacle Review: Dual High-Gain Powerhouses Tested Side-by-Side By Nina Harper July 10, 2026 Introduction: Two Distinct Paths to High-Gain Tone Wampler Pedals’ Super Plextortion and Pinnacle represent two philosophically divergent approaches to high-gain overdrive within the same product family. The Super Plextortion ($279 USD) is a meticulously voiced recreation of the legendary Plexi-era Marshall tones — specifically targeting the saturated midrange growl of a cranked ’68 Marshall Super Lead 100W head through a 4x12 cabinet loaded with Celestion G12M ‘Greenbacks’. The Pinnacle ($299 USD), by contrast, is a modern high-headroom distortion designed for tight low-end response, articulate note separation, and dynamic sensitivity — engineered to complement high-gain metal and progressive rock rigs without sacrificing touch responsiveness. Both are true-bypass, analog circuits housed in CNC-machined aluminum enclosures measuring 4.75" × 3.75" × 2.0", weighing 1.2 lbs each, and powered by standard 9V DC (center-negative) with a current draw of 22mA (Super Plextortion) and 24mA (Pinnacle). Over six weeks of daily testing across three guitar/amp combinations — a 1963 Fender Stratocaster into a 1978 Marshall JCM800 2203, a 2015 Gibson Les Paul Standard through a Friedman BE-100, and a PRS SE Custom 24 into a Fender Twin Reverb — these pedals revealed nuanced differences in harmonic complexity, compression behavior, and pedalboard integration. Circuit Architecture & Design Philosophy Under the hood, both pedals employ discrete transistor-based gain stages rather than op-amp ICs, preserving organic clipping characteristics and minimizing phase inversion artifacts. The Super Plextortion uses a three-stage JFET-driven topology inspired by the cascading preamp section of a non-master-volume Marshall. Its first stage features a dual-ganged J201 JFET configured for soft asymmetrical clipping; the second stage adds a 2N5457 JFET with adjustable bias via the ‘Tone’ pot; and the third stage employs a matched pair of 2N5459s for output saturation. This architecture deliberately emulates the voltage sag and natural compression of tube-driven signal paths — a key reason why it responds so authentically to guitar volume roll-off (tested from 10 to 3.5 on a 500kΩ CTS pot). Super Plextortion: The Analog Emulation Approach The Super Plextortion’s signal path includes a passive tone stack derived directly from Marshall’s original Baxandall-style EQ network, implemented with 1% metal-film resistors and polypropylene film capacitors (including a 0.022µF Orange Drop coupling cap between stages). Its ‘Gain’ control sweeps from clean boost (at 1–2 o’clock) through classic Plexi crunch (3–5) to full-blown lead saturation (7–10). Crucially, the ‘Volume’ knob is post-clipping but pre-EQ, meaning tone shaping remains consistent regardless of output level — a design choice that preserves midrange focus even at unity gain settings. Pinnacle: The Modern High-Fidelity Engine The Pinnacle departs significantly from vintage emulation. Its four-stage gain structure combines JFETs and silicon diodes in a hybrid clipping configuration: Stages one and two use matched 2SK372 JFETs for low-noise pre-saturation; stage three introduces symmetrical silicon clipping (1N4148 diodes) for aggressive harmonics; and stage four utilizes a proprietary buffered output stage with active EQ feedback. Unlike most high-gain pedals, the Pinnacle’s ‘Drive’ control doesn’t simply increase gain — it dynamically adjusts clipping threshold *and* low-end tightness via an internal 18V virtual rail circuit (achievable with the included Wampler Triple Tap power supply or any isolated 18V DC source). In stock Ratsbane quantity Add to cart Watch video Overview Features Videos Technical Downloads In stock Ratsbane quantity Add to cart “The Ratsbane is sort of my “tribute” to the original Rat circuit, incorporating how I mod the circuit.” Right facing | Front | Back | Left facing | Top |' data-navmenu="off" data-hashurl="off" data-menuSlider="off" data-continue-autoplay="off" data-outside-nav="off" data-autoplay="off" > 4 5 If you are looking for a single pedal solution with multiple degrees of gain from light overdrive to full out saturated fuzz tones, then you’ll surely love the Ratsbane. The Ratsbane is based on a true benchmark sound amongst guitarists that has been heard on thousands of famous recordings. The full, dynamic range, and sheer sonic force of this circuit is what makes it a true king amongst distortion pedals. Turn the distortion control all the way down for a deep but powerful gain booster. Crank it up and you will find rich harmonic overtones and a throaty, fuzz-like distortion. The “secret sauce” for this circuit has always been the filter control. Turn it counter-clockwise to cut straight through the mix with precision and high-frequency attack that lets your tone soar with absolute clarity. Turn it clockwise to filter the top end, for a warm, buttery, yet clear tone. This natural full-range distortion, mixed with its unique filter control, delivers a classic cranked tube-amp sound that crosses genres and generations of music. In typical Wampler fashion, Brian improved the circuit’s flexibility by adding two new switches. The Gain switch offers three distinct choices. In the middle gives you the “stock” gain for this pedal. Flick it either right or left for 2 additional turbocharged gain stages you can play with. The left position offers a firm, yet smooth boost in gain, whereas the right delivers an insane level of creamy distortion. The Voice switch subtly alters the compression and clipping of this pedal. It tightens the distortion to be more manageable with greater levels of gain, while rolling back some of the fuzz qualities, to deliver a modern, high gain distortion. $ 149.97 In stock Ratsbane quantity Add to cart SKU: WMP-RDI-PED Categories: Distortion / Overdrive , Fuzz Tags: distortion , overdrive warning Cancer and Reproductive Harm www.p65warnings.ca.gov Three Gain Options Brian has incorporated some unique modifications into this circuit, easily accessed by the toggle switches. With the gain switch set in the center you get the classic circuit, flick it either right or left to get insane amounts of gain on tap. Classic and Modern Tones Not content with just modifying the gain stages, Brian also added a voice switch which totally changes this circuit into a modern, higher gain style distortion. This pedal can cover boosted overdrive tones, full on fuzz, and modern searing distortion tones in one small package. Swap the engine This circuit is based on a modern, and in our opinion more harmonically complex, operational amplifier IC, but we know there are some purists out there that will want to try it with an LM308 IC, so we put our “engine” in a socket to allow those adventurous DIY “modders” amongst you to have some fun.
